sites.operation: st.volatile.shared.u8 (SASS STS.U8 [R4], R5 at 0x01d0, line attributed to thread_store.cuh:284)

pair: (read block_reduce_raking.cuh:222 or :161) vs (write warp_reduce_smem.cuh:160 / thread_store.cuh:284); the record's access list has the two reads and one write, so the racing pair is {read, write}
thread_pair_example: block 0, driver <<<1,65>>>: RAKING_THREADS=22, SEGMENT_LENGTH=3, WarpReduceSmem (22 is not a power of two). Lane 1 reads raking_grid bytes buff[3..5] (L222 then L161) while lane 4 writes reduce[4] = buff[4] (volatile store, first ReduceStep) with no warp-level synchronisation in between (the bug); both lanes are in warp 0.
class_reason: plain ld.shared against a volatile (strong) st.shared: a conflicting pair of which only one access is strong is a data race (not strong-vs-strong), D20.
buggy_expected: the pair is reported as a data race (DR), intra-warp, shared space, on the aliased raking_grid/warp_storage bytes; a detector that orders intra-warp lanes by lock-step would miss it (independent thread scheduling / PTX has no such ordering).

fixed.reason: the fix inserts WARP_SYNC(0x3fffff) (mask = (1<<RAKING_THREADS)-1) after the raking reads and before the WarpReduce call (block_reduce_raking.cuh, +5 lines); the later ReduceStep accesses are volatile but separated by their own WARP_SYNC(member_mask). SASS of the fixed build shows BRA.CONV UR6 + CALL $__cuda_sm70_warpsync with UR6=0x3fffff (the WARPSYNC) before the first STS.U8 of thread_store.cuh:284.

sass_notes: buggy build, nvdisasm -g: LDS.U8 [R0] (block_reduce_raking.cuh:222, 0x00f0), @!P0 LDS.U8 [R0+0x1] and @!P1 LDS.U8 [R0+0x2] (:161, 0x0130/0x0140), STS.U8 [R4], R5 (thread_store.cuh:284, 0x01d0) preceded in program order by no WARPSYNC/BAR. The volatile store lowers to a plain STS.U8 and the volatile load to a plain LDS.U8 (thread_load.cuh:331): sm_89 shared volatile has no .STRONG token in SASS. Kernel symbol _Z19block_reduce_kernelPKhPh.
derived_from: verify.accesses + verify.thread_pair of eval/realworld/targets.jsonl (cccl-1), re-checked against cub/cub/block/specializations/block_reduce_raking.cuh and cub/cub/warp/specializations/warp_reduce_smem.cuh at 5e0f922 and against cuobjdump/nvdisasm -g of the built driver (eval/x_logs, harness/sassline.sh) on 2026-10-20
open_questions: Whether the detector, which reads SASS, can tell the volatile store from a plain one: sm_89 emits plain STS.U8/LDS.U8 for it, so a report will carry the DR class regardless of the volatile qualifier.

review.notes: Checked at 5e0f922. BlockRakingLayout<uint8_t,65>: MAX_RAKING_THREADS=min(65,32)=32, SEGMENT_LENGTH=(65+31)/32=3, RAKING_THREADS=(65+2)/3=22, USE_SEGMENT_PADDING=0 (3 is odd), UNGUARDED=(65%22==0)=false (cub/cub/block/block_raking_layout.cuh:86-110); RakingPtr = buff + tid*3 (:148). WarpReduce<uint8_t,22> is WarpReduceSmem because 22 is not a power of two (cub/cub/warp/warp_reduce.cuh:169,177-178); its _TempStorage begins with T reduce[38] (warp_reduce_smem.cuh:101-105) and BlockReduceRaking::_TempStorage is a union of warp_storage and raking_grid (block_reduce_raking.cuh:121-128), so reduce[4] is raking_grid.buff[4]. Lane 1 reads buff[3] (block_reduce_raking.cuh:222) and buff[4], buff[5] (:161; guard 1*3+ITER < 65 holds), lane 4 stores reduce[4] in the first ReduceStep (warp_reduce_smem.cuh:160 -> thread_store.cuh:284, volatile store); both lanes in warp 0. The only barrier, CTA_SYNC at block_reduce_raking.cuh:215, precedes both accesses; the first WARP_SYNC (warp_reduce_smem.cuh:162) comes after the store. Fix cb8707cb inserts WARP_SYNC((1<<RAKING_THREADS)-1) = 0x3fffff after :226, between the raking reads and the WarpReduce call; its second hunk (cub/cub/thread/thread_reduce.cuh) only renames Lenght -> Length. Every later ReduceStep access is separated by WARP_SYNC(member_mask) (warp_reduce_smem.cuh:162,171), so 'absent' holds. Driver driver.cu: BlockReduce<uint8_t,65,BLOCK_REDUCE_RAKING>::Sum in <<<1,65>>>. Class: a plain load against a volatile store is DR (CLAUDE.md T21 item 1); the pair is not strong-vs-strong, so D20 does not change it. sass_notes are the builder's: the reviewer read sources and diffs only and did not re-dump SASS (the one srun queued with an estimated start the next day and was withdrawn).
